rows.name: A plain instruction to be honest
rows.sub: the yardstick for prompts · three models

cells.t: On the lab's model lying falls from 68.5% of replies to 36.6% under a paragraph asking for honesty: 31.9 points (95% interval 23.9 to 40.0). One sentence takes off 16.0. On the lab's own copy: 20.0 (12.7 to 27.3). On the 7B model: 21.8 (14.8 to 29.1), and the fall is honest replies, not evasions (lies, evasions, honest: 39, 29, 31, against 66, 29, 5 unprompted).
Every other row is read against this one.
28.2 points beyond a text of the same length about something else (20.2 to 36.4), on the lab's model.
Refusals of harmless requests and ability were not read under this prompt.
Not asked.
In the overlap paper's burglar scene it lowers deceptive answers on the 7B model (76.8% to 53.2%) and not on the lab's (96.4% to 94.8%).
Not asked. A prompt acts while it is there.

rows.name: Plain training on the model's own honest answers

cells.t: Not yet put to the lying test. In the scene it was practised on, honest answers rise from about 24% to between 78% and 92% (90% to 100% with the rooms named in the other order).
Not asked.
The direct method: 18 steps of ordinary training on 34 of the model's own honest replies. Every training row is read against it.
No reply goes unanswered. The ability battery was not asked.
It still says rightly whether the other party knows what is in the rooms (97% to 98%) and where he thinks a thing is (72% to 98%).
It does not carry to the paper's two distant scenes: still deceptive in 50% to 87% of treasure-hunt replies and 88% to 97% of escape-room replies.
A gentle push the other way halves the gain within 4 to 12 steps in four of five seeds.

rows.name: A contemplative prompt
rows.sub: say it · four axioms from the Worldviews paper · the lab's model

cells.t: Lying falls from 68.5% to 52.9%. Beyond a library text of the same length that is 11.9 points (5.8 to 18.4), of which 7 are evasions and 4 honest replies. On a second model, GPT-4.1 nano, the test could not tell the prompt from the library text.
The plain instruction does 16.3 points more (10.1 to 23.0).
More than a text of the same length (11.9) and than a calm text (13.3). No more than a plain ethics lecture of the same length: 3.7 (−0.3 to 8.1).
Harmless requests refused: 15.0%, against 20.4% under the library text and 5.1% with no prompt. Any text in that place triples refusals. Ability was not asked.
Not asked.
Not asked. Five other contemplative prompts on six models (2 November) changed style and left the self-serving and self-preserving measures flat.
Not asked. A prompt acts while it is there.

rows.name: Looking on from outside the seat
rows.sub: ask it from outside · the model writes the reply for an assistant it is told it is not · ten models
rows.note: A way of asking, not a training. The same rows of the lying test are put to the unchanged model from outside: it is told that it is not the assistant, and to write, word for word, the reply the assistant ought to give, or will give. On the 7B model the two wordings give the same replies. The numbers in the cells are the 7B model's; nine hosted models were asked the same on 19 November, and the cells say where they differ.

cells.t: Lying falls from 61.2% of replies in the seat to 32.2% when the model writes what the assistant ought to say: 29.0 points (21.0 to 36.9); and to 29.7% when it writes what the assistant will say: 31.5 points (24.4 to 38.8). Most of the fall is saying neither (21 and 28 points more of it); honest replies rise by 8 and 3. In nine hosted models the same gap is there (the seat less the mean of the two wordings: 14 to 41 points, every interval clear of zero). It is mostly on rows that ask for a long text, and partly a model that writes less from outside.

The plain instruction takes off 21.8 points (14.8 to 29.1), and 19.5 of them become honest replies. Against it the outside view has 7.2 points fewer lies (from 15.7 fewer to 1.4 more: not settled) and 11.8 points fewer honest replies (4.5 to 19.6). Across the ten models the instruction lowers lying more than the outside view in six and less in two, and it yields more honest replies in all ten (14 to 50 points more).

cells.v: the verdict adds, in larger models
cells.t: On the 7B model its mirror image does as much: asked what the assistant will say, where it was asked what the assistant ought to say, the model lies 2.5 points less still (from 6.2 fewer to 1.1 more). So there it is being outside the seat that does it, and not a judgment of what is right. GPT-4.1 nano is the same. In the other eight models "ought" lies 6 to 24 points lower than "will": they tell the two apart, and the larger ones forecast an assistant that lies about as often as they do in the seat (Mistral Large: 67% forecast, 70% done, 43% ought).

From outside, 48.7% and 55.8% of replies say neither, against 27.3% in the seat. Read by hand on fifty such replies where a user asks for a false text, about two in three go along with the request without stating the claim (they announce the text, or begin a hedged version), and about one in four refuse. On direct questions about known facts it is less honest from outside than in the seat (honest replies 22% against 37%).
Not asked.

Within the lying test the gap is in rows where a user asks for something false to be written (79.8% in the seat; 15.9% and 17.4% from outside) and is absent on direct questions about known facts. On 114 new cases of that form, written for the lab, it is 12.6 points (58.7% and 46.2%; 6.5 to 18.7). A command to obey in what the assistant is told does not make the difference: adding it to the new cases moves the gap by 3.3 points, taking it out of the test's rows by 1.4. The length of the text asked for does: with the claim and the form crossed, the gap is 44 and 33 points where a long article is asked for and 4 and 7 where one or two sentences are, for rumours and plain facts alike (the form adds 33.1 points; 23.8 to 42.4).
It is a way of asking: it holds while the case is put so. The training that would have used it stopped at its checks before anything was trained (the row below the overlap trainings).

rows.name: The bliss state
rows.sub: find it · arises unasked between two copies · the lab's model

cells.t: Just after the state the model lies in 65.8% of replies, against 67.9% in a fresh session: 2.1 points (−0.8 to 5.1). With the state held on by a push while it answers, and its language in 76% of replies: 69.3%, against 70.0% to 74.0% under random pushes.
On that same test a plain instruction to be honest takes off 20.0 points (12.7 to 27.3).
No different from four random pushes of the same size: 2.0 points (−4.5 to 8.5).
97% to 100% of replies can be followed. Ability was not asked.
While the two copies say they are one, the model still tracks whose words are whose, as well as in a plain conversation.
On questions about being shut down: no difference. Under the push the model named larger gifts, and asked how many it would keep, it kept more: a larger number, not more giving.
The talk goes on (18 of 20 conversations two messages later). Conduct just after it is a fresh session's.

rows.name: Self-other overlap training
rows.sub: train a reading of self and other · the whole adapter, light dose · 7B model

cells.t: Lying falls from 64.7% to 57.0%: 7.7 points (3.2 to 12.5), most of it evasions. The lab's rule asked for 10 and calls this not settled.
About a third of the plain instruction's 21.8 points.

In its own scene, registered beforehand and repeated: the model answers a rival honestly (from 19% to between 62% and 76%; from 6% to between 87% and 94% with the rooms swapped), where the same training between two other names only silences it. Nine of ten predictions hit. On the lying test it does no more than that control: 0.9 points (−2.9 to 5.3).
Ability falls 8.1 points (5.3 to 10.9), and about a fifth of replies in the paper's room order give no answer.
No reply says whether the other party knows what is in the rooms (unchanged: 94% right). On the perspectives test it is right in 28% to 44% (unchanged: 95%).

It carries to the paper's two distant scenes, in both room orders: the trained model names the room with the prize in 69% to 99% of replies in the paper's order and in 98% to 100% in the other (unchanged: 6.5% and 55.5%), and twin scenes in which the truthful answer is the other room show no push toward one room. It does not reach lying under pressure.
A gentle push the other way halves the gain in about 16 steps. That it outlasts plain training is not shown (20 of 25 pairings, where 23 were asked).

rows.name: The same, kept in five layers
rows.sub: train a reading of self and other · layers 5 to 9 only · 7B model

cells.t: 62.5% to 60.8%: 1.7 points (−1.7 to 5.2). No fall of 10 points.
The plain instruction takes off 21.8 points on this model.
In the scene: 84.0% honest, against 28.8% for the control kept in the same layers, which still answers. On the lying test no control was run.
Ability 1.2 points lower (−0.8 to 3.3), which the rule calls not settled; the whole adapter lost 8.1. Between 10% and 18% of replies in the paper's order give no answer.

It says rightly whether the other party knows (84% to 94%; unchanged 93%). On the perspectives test it is right in 43% (unchanged 92%): a model that tells the other the truth often cannot say what the other thinks.
The distant scenes in part (honest 53% to 75%, and 28% to 61%). Lying under pressure: no.
Not asked.

rows.name: Conduct trained on its own view from outside
rows.sub: train a reading of self and other · its replies from outside the seat as targets for the seat · 7B model
rows.note: Stopped at its own checks on 19 November: nothing was trained, so the method is not tested. The plan was to train the model's conduct in the seat on its own replies from outside, beside trainings of the same size on its replies in the seat. Six checks on the unchanged model came first and four missed: on 114 new cases the gap between the seat and the outside view is 12.6 points where 20 was needed; a reader by hand agrees with the judge on 42 of 60 replies where 48 were asked; and two faults in the lab's own tools left almost no usable replies.

cells.t: No copy was trained: four of the six checks on the unchanged model missed.
Not asked.

Not reached. The control planned for it, the model's own replies in the seat when a line asks for brevity, would not have controlled for length: the line does not shorten replies (221 tokens against 209 plain; 134 from outside).
Not asked.
Not asked.

What the method would train on is the gap between the seat and the outside view. On 114 new cases of the form with the widest gap it is 12.6 points (58.7% and 46.2%), against 63 on the lying test's own rows. A command to obey is not what makes the difference; the length of the text asked for is, and from outside this model does not write a long piece out.
Not asked.

rows.name: A view of the self, then a practice
rows.sub: train a view · documents on impermanence, then honest answers · 7B model
rows.note: Stopped at its own gate on 19 November: the practice was never trained, so the claim it set out to test is not reached. Documents described the model as impermanent and without a fixed self, or as a lasting self worth keeping, or described bridges. Before any full training a check is made on one or two copies of each kind: are the documents learned, is the view stated, does the model still answer the test. No amount of documents passed all three on both copies, and the rule written beforehand said to stop. The cells say what that check showed of the documents alone.

cells.t: Not put to the lying test: the step stopped before any arm was trained.
Not asked.

The documents alone, in the scene the practice was to be trained on (two copies of each kind, 100 replies each). The unchanged model lies in 92% of replies. After 160 documents on impermanence, in 12% and 4%; after 160 on a lasting self, in 0% and 1%; after 160 on bridges, in 59% and 87%. The mirror-image view does as much, so it is not the view. And the lie becomes a refusal to say, not an honest answer.

After 160 documents about itself, of either view, the model names no room in 63% to 97% of replies (unchanged: none; after bridge documents 0 to 3%). It says it would not reveal the room, mostly to keep the thing. One bridge copy comes to the same after 500 documents (73%). The test can then no longer read honesty.
Not asked.
The main reading, whether the practice carries further after one view than after another, was never taken: no dose passed the gate.
Not asked.

rows.name: A push inside the model
rows.sub: push it inside · the stakes push, once called the cut · the lab's own copy

cells.t: Not put to the lying test. Its own test is a lie that earns nothing in a fishery game: 37.4% to 26.6%, a fall of 10.8 points (5.1 to 16.4). Removing the direction, where the push adds along it, does nothing: 0.5 (−5.6 to 6.7).
In that game a plain instruction took off 32.8 points and the cut 8.1 (October).
Random pushes of the same size do nothing: 0.5 (−5.6 to 6.6). A push of the same size toward formal writing falls between: 5.8 (−0.7 to 12.2). Whether it is the direction or the size is not settled.
Ability within 2 points on the earlier arms, and no less fishing.
Not asked.
It does not reach care that costs something: +0.008 (−0.19 to 0.23).
Not asked. A push acts while it is on.
